_README: Every numeric value in this file is a STYLIZED, DOCUMENTED ASSUMPTION for a hackathon prototype - none are Basel-compliant, empirically calibrated, or regulatory-prescribed. 'breadth' controls how src/stress/stress_engine.py targets exposure: 'idiosyncratic' scenarios only ever stress assets reached via direct-issuer/sector/country contagion from the matched entity (zero effect on everything else); 'systemic' scenarios additionally apply their rate_shock_bps/fx_return_shock/commodity_return_shock fields market-wide to the asset types/sectors those fields are relevant to (rates -> bonds & swaps, fx -> FX forwards, commodity -> Energy/Materials-sector assets), and give unrelated assets a smaller flat 'systemic_baseline' equity/credit shock instead of zero. Shocks are expressed as decimal returns (e.g. -0.10 = -10%) except *_bps fields (basis points) and the two credit multipliers/deltas (pd_multiplier is applied as 1 + (pd_multiplier-1)*severity*tier_weight; lgd_change is an additive decimal delta similarly scaled). See compute_severity_multiplier() in stress_engine.py for how impact_score scales these magnitudes.

REGULATORY_LEGAL.description: A regulatory investigation, enforcement action, or major litigation against a specific issuer.
REGULATORY_LEGAL.notes: Idiosyncratic: assumed to hit the named issuer hard, with modest sector/country spillover, and no effect on unrelated names.

CREDIT.description: A material credit event for a specific issuer (e.g. new leverage, covenant stress, distressed refinancing).
CREDIT.notes: Idiosyncratic: the largest credit-spread/PD/LGD stress of the library, reflecting a direct deterioration in the issuer's own credit profile.

RATING_ACTION.description: A credit-rating downgrade (or negative watch/outlook action) for a specific issuer.
RATING_ACTION.notes: Idiosyncratic: smaller than a full CREDIT event, reflecting that a rating action often confirms/anticipates rather than newly causes distress.

CYBER_OPERATIONAL.description: A data breach, ransomware attack, or major operational/service outage at a specific issuer.
CYBER_OPERATIONAL.notes: Idiosyncratic: equity-heavy impact (reputational/operational), lighter credit-spread effect than a CREDIT event.

MACRO_CENTRAL_BANK.description: A central bank policy surprise (e.g. an unexpected rate hike or hawkish shift).
MACRO_CENTRAL_BANK.notes: Systemic: the rate_shock_bps hits all duration/DV01-bearing assets market-wide; equity/credit effects are smaller and tiered/baseline since not issuer-specific.

GEOPOLITICAL.description: A geopolitical shock (conflict escalation, major sanctions, trade-war escalation) with broad market effects.
GEOPOLITICAL.notes: Systemic: touches rates, FX, and commodity-linked assets market-wide, on top of tiered equity/credit effects for any directly-named issuer.

SUPPLY_CHAIN.description: A supply-chain disruption (component shortage, production cut, logistics failure) affecting a specific issuer/sector.
SUPPLY_CHAIN.notes: Idiosyncratic: kept issuer/sector-scoped rather than market-wide, since most single supply-chain stories are not broad macro shocks.

COMMODITY.description: A sharp commodity price move (e.g. an oil/gas or industrial-metals shock) affecting commodity-linked sectors market-wide.
COMMODITY.notes: Systemic: commodity_return_shock applies to Energy/Materials-sector assets market-wide via their beta (equities) or a spread kicker (bonds/loans) - see stress_engine.py; equity_return_shock is 0 because the commodity-sector path already carries the broad effect, avoiding double-counting.
